question: What is the main purpose of a gravity sewer in a wastewater collection system?
correctAnswer: To carry wastewater by gravity from higher ground to a lower outlet
explanation: A gravity sewer is installed on a slope so that wastewater flows downhill by gravity to an outlet, lift station, or treatment plant without pumping.
options: To pump wastewater uphill to a treatment plant
To carry wastewater by gravity from higher ground to a lower outlet
To store wastewater until it can be treated
To filter solids out of the wastewater
optionA: To pump wastewater uphill to a treatment plant
optionB: To carry wastewater by gravity from higher ground to a lower outlet
optionC: To store wastewater until it can be treated
optionD: To filter solids out of the wastewater
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Gravity Sewers and Manholes. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why are manholes installed along a gravity sewer?
correctAnswer: To provide access for inspection, cleaning, and maintenance
explanation: Manholes are access structures. They let operators inspect the sewer, set up cleaning and CCTV equipment, and reach the pipe for maintenance and repair.
options: To provide access for inspection, cleaning, and maintenance
To add oxygen to the wastewater
To increase the pressure in the sewer
To connect household plumbing directly to the main
optionA: To provide access for inspection, cleaning, and maintenance
optionB: To add oxygen to the wastewater
optionC: To increase the pressure in the sewer
optionD: To connect household plumbing directly to the main
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Gravity Sewers and Manholes. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Maintain & Restore Collection System: Gravity Sewers and Manholes

question: Manholes are normally placed at which locations along a sewer?
correctAnswer: At changes in direction, grade, or pipe size, and at junctions
explanation: Manholes are placed where the sewer changes direction, slope, or size, and where branch sewers join, so every change point can be reached for inspection and cleaning.
options: Only at the lowest point of the system
Only where two streets intersect
At changes in direction, grade, or pipe size, and at junctions
At every individual house connection
optionA: Only at the lowest point of the system
optionB: Only where two streets intersect
optionC: At changes in direction, grade, or pipe size, and at junctions
optionD: At every individual house connection
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Gravity Sewers and Manholes. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: In a manhole, what does the term invert refer to?
correctAnswer: The lowest inside point of the pipe or channel where flow passes
explanation: The invert is the lowest point inside the pipe or manhole channel. Invert elevations are used to set and check the slope of a sewer.
options: The top rim of the manhole frame
The lowest inside point of the pipe or channel where flow passes
The underside of the manhole cover
The highest point of the pipe crown
optionA: The top rim of the manhole frame
optionB: The lowest inside point of the pipe or channel where flow passes
optionC: The underside of the manhole cover
optionD: The highest point of the pipe crown
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Why is a gravity sewer pipe installed on a continuous downward slope?
correctAnswer: So flow keeps moving and carries solids toward the outlet instead of settling
explanation: The slope gives the flow enough energy to keep solids suspended and moving. On a flat or back graded reach, solids settle and blockages form.
options: So rainwater can drain out of the pipe joints
So the pipe can be installed without manholes
So wastewater stays in the pipe longer for treatment
So flow keeps moving and carries solids toward the outlet instead of settling
optionA: So rainwater can drain out of the pipe joints
optionB: So the pipe can be installed without manholes
optionC: So wastewater stays in the pipe longer for treatment
optionD: So flow keeps moving and carries solids toward the outlet instead of settling
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Gravity Sewers and Manholes. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the main job of a wastewater lift station?
correctAnswer: To raise wastewater to a higher elevation so it can flow on by gravity
explanation: A lift station is used where gravity flow is not possible. Its pumps raise the wastewater to a higher elevation so gravity flow can resume.
options: To raise wastewater to a higher elevation so it can flow on by gravity
To screen rags and debris out of wastewater
To disinfect wastewater before discharge
To measure the flow in a gravity sewer
optionA: To raise wastewater to a higher elevation so it can flow on by gravity
optionB: To screen rags and debris out of wastewater
optionC: To disinfect wastewater before discharge
optionD: To measure the flow in a gravity sewer
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Lift Station Components. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Where does incoming wastewater collect in a lift station before it is pumped?
correctAnswer: In the wet well
explanation: Incoming gravity sewers discharge into the wet well, a storage chamber where wastewater collects until the pumps start and send it into the force main.
options: In the force main
In the valve chamber
In the wet well
In the surge tank
optionA: In the force main
optionB: In the valve chamber
optionC: In the wet well
optionD: In the surge tank
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Lift Station Components. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the purpose of the check valve on a pump discharge line?
correctAnswer: To stop pumped wastewater from flowing back into the wet well when the pump stops
explanation: When a pump stops, the water column in the discharge line and force main would drain back into the wet well. The check valve closes to prevent that reverse flow.
options: To let air escape from the force main
To stop pumped wastewater from flowing back into the wet well when the pump stops
To measure the pump discharge pressure
To mix the wastewater in the wet well
optionA: To let air escape from the force main
optionB: To stop pumped wastewater from flowing back into the wet well when the pump stops
optionC: To measure the pump discharge pressure
optionD: To mix the wastewater in the wet well
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Lift Station Components. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: On a submersible pump installation, what do the guide rails allow the operator to do?
correctAnswer: Raise and lower the pump for service without entering the wet well
explanation: Submersible pumps ride on guide rails so they can be lifted to the surface for inspection and service, and lowered back onto the discharge connection, without anyone entering the wet well.
options: Adjust the pump speed from the surface
Guide wastewater into the pump intake
Hold the level floats at the right depth
Raise and lower the pump for service without entering the wet well
optionA: Adjust the pump speed from the surface
optionB: Guide wastewater into the pump intake
optionC: Hold the level floats at the right depth
optionD: Raise and lower the pump for service without entering the wet well
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: What does a high level alarm in a lift station tell the operator?
correctAnswer: The wet well level is abnormally high and needs attention before an overflow occurs
explanation: The high level alarm warns that wastewater has risen above the normal operating range, giving operators a chance to respond before sewage backs up or overflows.
options: The wet well level is abnormally high and needs attention before an overflow occurs
The pump motor has reached its service interval
The force main pressure is too low
The station has lost its ventilation
optionA: The wet well level is abnormally high and needs attention before an overflow occurs
optionB: The pump motor has reached its service interval
optionC: The force main pressure is too low
optionD: The station has lost its ventilation

question: A pump starts and stops every few minutes all day, even at low inflow, and the floats are working properly. What is the most likely cause?
correctAnswer: The pump on and pump off levels are set too close together, leaving too little operating volume
explanation: With the on and off levels close together, the pump empties the small operating volume quickly and inflow refills it quickly. The resulting short cycling causes frequent starts that wear the motor and starter.
options: The force main is too long
The inflow is too steady
The pump on and pump off levels are set too close together, leaving too little operating volume
The check valve is holding pressure
optionA: The force main is too long
optionB: The inflow is too steady
optionC: The pump on and pump off levels are set too close together, leaving too little operating volume
optionD: The check valve is holding pressure
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Wet Wells and Level Control. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: In a duplex lift station, why do the pumps alternate as lead pump after each cycle?
correctAnswer: To even out run hours and wear so both pumps stay exercised and share the work
explanation: Alternating the lead pump after each cycle equalizes run time and wear, and it keeps both pumps exercised so a standby pump is ready when needed.
options: To keep one pump permanently out of service
To even out run hours and wear so both pumps stay exercised and share the work
To double the station discharge pressure
To prevent the wet well from ever filling
optionA: To keep one pump permanently out of service
optionB: To even out run hours and wear so both pumps stay exercised and share the work
optionC: To double the station discharge pressure
optionD: To prevent the wet well from ever filling
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Wet Wells and Level Control. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A float switch coated with grease fails to signal a pump start. What is the most likely result if the failure is not caught?
correctAnswer: The wet well level keeps rising toward a high level alarm, backup, or overflow
explanation: A grease fouled float cannot signal the control panel to start the pump, so inflow keeps raising the level until a high level alarm, a backup, or an overflow results.
options: The wet well level keeps rising toward a high level alarm, backup, or overflow
The pump runs dry and burns out
The force main drains back into the street
The station discharge flow doubles
optionA: The wet well level keeps rising toward a high level alarm, backup, or overflow
optionB: The pump runs dry and burns out
optionC: The force main drains back into the street
optionD: The station discharge flow doubles
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Wet Wells and Level Control. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: The lead pump is running but the wet well level continues to rise and the lag pump starts. What does this most likely indicate?
correctAnswer: Inflow is greater than one pump can handle, or the lead pump output has fallen
explanation: When one pump cannot lower the level, either inflow exceeds its capacity or the pump is underperforming, for example from a worn impeller or a partly blocked discharge, so the lag pump is called in.
options: The floats are set at the wrong elevations
The station is drawing too much power
The wet well is too large for the station
Inflow is greater than one pump can handle, or the lead pump output has fallen
optionA: The floats are set at the wrong elevations
optionB: The station is drawing too much power
optionC: The wet well is too large for the station
optionD: Inflow is greater than one pump can handle, or the lead pump output has fallen
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Wet Wells and Level Control. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A pressure transducer at the bottom of a wet well is used to control pump operation. How does it sense level?
correctAnswer: It measures the pressure of the wastewater column above it, which increases with depth
explanation: The transducer senses the pressure exerted by the liquid above it. Pressure rises in direct proportion to depth, so the control system converts the pressure reading into a level.
options: It counts the bubbles rising through the wastewater
It measures the pressure of the wastewater column above it, which increases with depth
It weighs the wastewater in the wet well
It measures the speed of the incoming flow
optionA: It counts the bubbles rising through the wastewater
optionB: It measures the pressure of the wastewater column above it, which increases with depth
optionC: It weighs the wastewater in the wet well
optionD: It measures the speed of the incoming flow
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: What is a force main?
correctAnswer: A pipe that carries wastewater under pressure from a lift station to a discharge point
explanation: A force main is the pressurized discharge pipe of a lift station. Unlike a gravity sewer, it can carry wastewater uphill because the pump provides the pressure.
options: A large gravity sewer that carries peak wet weather flow
A pipe used only for flushing water
A pipe that carries wastewater under pressure from a lift station to a discharge point
The suction pipe inside a wet well
optionA: A large gravity sewer that carries peak wet weather flow
optionB: A pipe used only for flushing water
optionC: A pipe that carries wastewater under pressure from a lift station to a discharge point
optionD: The suction pipe inside a wet well
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Force Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why are air release valves installed at high points on a force main?
correctAnswer: To release trapped air that would otherwise collect, restrict flow, and reduce pumping capacity
explanation: Air rises to high points in a force main and collects there. A working air release valve vents that air, preventing an air pocket from narrowing the flow path and adding head loss.
options: To release trapped air that would otherwise collect, restrict flow, and reduce pumping capacity
To add air so solids stay in suspension
To relieve the wet well of odours
To drain the force main for cleaning
optionA: To release trapped air that would otherwise collect, restrict flow, and reduce pumping capacity
optionB: To add air so solids stay in suspension
optionC: To relieve the wet well of odours
optionD: To drain the force main for cleaning
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Force Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Maintain & Restore Collection System: Force Mains

question: Why is very low velocity in a force main a problem during long low flow periods?
correctAnswer: Solids can settle out and gases can form, leading to deposits, odours, and corrosion
explanation: At low velocity, solids are no longer kept in suspension and settle in the pipe. Stagnant wastewater also generates gases such as hydrogen sulfide, which drive odour and corrosion problems.
options: The pipe pressure rises above the pump rating
The wastewater becomes too cold to pump
The check valves wear out faster
Solids can settle out and gases can form, leading to deposits, odours, and corrosion
optionA: The pipe pressure rises above the pump rating
optionB: The wastewater becomes too cold to pump
optionC: The check valves wear out faster
optionD: Solids can settle out and gases can form, leading to deposits, odours, and corrosion
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

blueprintObjective: Monitor, Evaluate & Adjust Collection System: Force Mains

question: A lift station pump runs normally but discharge flow has slowly fallen over several weeks. Which cause should be checked first at the force main high point?
correctAnswer: An air pocket trapped at the high point because the air release valve is not working
explanation: Air collects at the high point when the release valve fails, and the growing air pocket restricts flow area and adds friction loss, so delivered flow falls even though the pump itself runs normally.
options: A float switch coated with grease
An air pocket trapped at the high point because the air release valve is not working
A rain gauge reading too high
A manhole cover left open upstream
optionA: A float switch coated with grease
optionB: An air pocket trapped at the high point because the air release valve is not working
optionC: A rain gauge reading too high
optionD: A manhole cover left open upstream
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Force Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What can happen in a force main when a pump stops suddenly?
correctAnswer: A pressure surge, or water hammer, can travel through the pipe and damage pipes or fittings
explanation: A sudden stoppage of moving water in a pressure pipe creates a surge wave. The pressure spike can burst pipes or damage joints, valves, and fittings if it is not controlled.
options: The wastewater instantly freezes in the pipe
The wet well empties by siphon action
A pressure surge, or water hammer, can travel through the pipe and damage pipes or fittings
Solids dissolve back into the flow
optionA: The wastewater instantly freezes in the pipe
optionB: The wet well empties by siphon action
optionC: A pressure surge, or water hammer, can travel through the pipe and damage pipes or fittings
optionD: Solids dissolve back into the flow
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: What is the main purpose of flow monitoring in a collection system?
correctAnswer: To measure how much wastewater flows at a point so capacity, trends, and problems can be assessed
explanation: Flow data show how much wastewater a part of the system carries. Operators use it to judge remaining capacity, spot abnormal flows such as I&I, and plan cleaning, repair, and upgrades.
options: To measure how much wastewater flows at a point so capacity, trends, and problems can be assessed
To remove grit from the wastewater
To control the speed of the lift station pumps directly
To disinfect flow before it reaches the plant
optionA: To measure how much wastewater flows at a point so capacity, trends, and problems can be assessed
optionB: To remove grit from the wastewater
optionC: To control the speed of the lift station pumps directly

question: An area velocity flow meter installed in a sewer calculates flow from which two measurements?
correctAnswer: The depth of flow and the average velocity of the flow
explanation: An area velocity meter measures the depth of flow to get the flow area and senses average velocity. Flow is then calculated as area multiplied by velocity.
options: The pipe pressure and the water temperature
The rainfall depth and the pipe diameter only
The pump run time and the wet well size
The depth of flow and the average velocity of the flow
optionA: The pipe pressure and the water temperature
optionB: The rainfall depth and the pipe diameter only
optionC: The pump run time and the wet well size
optionD: The depth of flow and the average velocity of the flow

question: A portable flume inserted in a manhole channel measures flow by relating which reading to a known flow table?
correctAnswer: The depth of water passing through the flume
explanation: A flume narrows the flow in a known shape, so the measured upstream depth corresponds to a specific flow rate in the flume rating table.
options: The colour of the wastewater
The depth of water passing through the flume
The weight of the flume insert
The speed of the surface ripples only
optionA: The colour of the wastewater
optionB: The depth of water passing through the flume
optionC: The weight of the flume insert

question: Flow at a monitoring site is steady on dry days but jumps sharply within an hour of rainfall starting. What does this pattern most strongly suggest?
correctAnswer: Rainfall dependent inflow is entering the system through direct connections or defects
explanation: A fast flow response timed with rainfall is the signature of inflow, since groundwater infiltration changes slowly. Direct connections such as roof leaders, sump pumps, and leaking covers in ponded areas admit stormwater quickly.
options: The treatment plant is discharging to the sewer
Groundwater levels are falling
Rainfall dependent inflow is entering the system through direct connections or defects
A pump station upstream has been shut off
optionA: The treatment plant is discharging to the sewer
optionB: Groundwater levels are falling
optionC: Rainfall dependent inflow is entering the system through direct connections or defects
optionD: A pump station upstream has been shut off

question: Why is a rain gauge installed near a flow monitoring site during an infiltration and inflow study?
correctAnswer: So flow changes can be matched against rainfall to separate wet weather response from dry weather flow
explanation: Rainfall records let analysts compare flow before, during, and after storms. The size and timing of the flow increase relative to rainfall shows how much wet weather water is entering the system.
options: So flow changes can be matched against rainfall to separate wet weather response from dry weather flow
To keep the flow meter electronics dry
To measure the flow in open channels nearby
To trigger the meter to start recording
optionA: So flow changes can be matched against rainfall to separate wet weather response from dry weather flow
optionB: To keep the flow meter electronics dry
optionC: To measure the flow in open channels nearby
optionD: To trigger the meter to start recording

question: Which statement correctly describes infiltration?
correctAnswer: Groundwater entering the sewer through cracks, defective joints, and other defects
explanation: Infiltration is groundwater that leaks into the sewer through defects in pipes, joints, laterals, and manholes. It rises and falls with the groundwater table rather than with individual storms.
options: Stormwater entering through roof leaders and sump pumps
Wastewater leaking out of a surcharged sewer
Rainwater ponding on manhole covers
Groundwater entering the sewer through cracks, defective joints, and other defects
optionA: Stormwater entering through roof leaders and sump pumps
optionB: Wastewater leaking out of a surcharged sewer
optionC: Rainwater ponding on manhole covers
optionD: Groundwater entering the sewer through cracks, defective joints, and other defects
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Which of the following is a source of inflow rather than infiltration?
correctAnswer: A residential sump pump discharge connected to the sanitary sewer
explanation: Sump pumps are a direct connection that delivers storm related water straight into the sanitary system, which is inflow. Cracks and leaking joints below the water table admit groundwater, which is infiltration.
options: A cracked clay pipe below the water table
A residential sump pump discharge connected to the sanitary sewer
A leaking manhole wall joint
A defective lateral connection seal
optionA: A cracked clay pipe below the water table
optionB: A residential sump pump discharge connected to the sanitary sewer
optionC: A leaking manhole wall joint
optionD: A defective lateral connection seal
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Infiltration and Inflow Sources. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: During a period of high groundwater, which defect is most likely to add infiltration to a sewer?
correctAnswer: Open or displaced pipe joints below the water table
explanation: Joints that are open or displaced below the water table give groundwater a direct path into the pipe. High groundwater raises the pressure driving that infiltration.
options: A vented manhole cover on high ground
A roof leader connected to a storm sewer
Open or displaced pipe joints below the water table
A sealed and bolted manhole frame
optionA: A vented manhole cover on high ground
optionB: A roof leader connected to a storm sewer
optionC: Open or displaced pipe joints below the water table
optionD: A sealed and bolted manhole frame
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: What is an operational effect of excessive infiltration and inflow on a collection system?
correctAnswer: Higher flows that can surcharge sewers, overload lift stations, and cause overflows or backups
explanation: Extra I&I water consumes pipe and pump capacity meant for sanitary flow. In wet weather it can surcharge sewers and lift stations, leading to basement backups and overflows, and it raises pumping and treatment costs.
options: Higher flows that can surcharge sewers, overload lift stations, and cause overflows or backups
Lower flows that starve the treatment plant
Cleaner wastewater that needs no treatment
Reduced wear on all pumps and pipes
optionA: Higher flows that can surcharge sewers, overload lift stations, and cause overflows or backups
optionB: Lower flows that starve the treatment plant
optionC: Cleaner wastewater that needs no treatment
optionD: Reduced wear on all pumps and pipes
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Dry weather flows in a sewershed stay well above expected sanitary flow for weeks while groundwater is high, with little change between day and night. What is the most likely explanation?
correctAnswer: Steady groundwater infiltration through pipe and manhole defects
explanation: A steady, day and night elevation in dry weather flow that tracks high groundwater points to infiltration through defects, because inflow sources respond to rainfall events rather than staying constant.
options: Roof leaders discharging during storms
A one time spill upstream
Sump pumps cycling during rain
Steady groundwater infiltration through pipe and manhole defects

optionB: A one time spill upstream

question: A sewer reach is partly blocked by heavy grease deposits. Which cleaning approach is most appropriate as a first step?
correctAnswer: Hydraulic jetting with a nozzle suited to grease, working from the downstream manhole and removing debris at that manhole
explanation: Jetting with a grease cutting nozzle scours deposits from the pipe wall, and working from the downstream manhole lets the flow carry loosened material back to that manhole, where it can be vacuumed out instead of moving the problem downstream.
options: Pushing the grease downstream with a flush of water and leaving it in the next reach
Hydraulic jetting with a nozzle suited to grease, working from the downstream manhole and removing debris at that manhole
Sealing the reach and filling it with drinking water
Cutting the pipe open at the blockage as the first step
optionA: Pushing the grease downstream with a flush of water and leaving it in the next reach
optionB: Hydraulic jetting with a nozzle suited to grease, working from the downstream manhole and removing debris at that manhole
optionC: Sealing the reach and filling it with drinking water
optionD: Cutting the pipe open at the blockage as the first step
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Sewer Cleaning Methods. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: When is a bucket machine the better choice over jetting?
correctAnswer: In a large sewer with heavy deposits of sand, gravel, and debris that jetting cannot move effectively
explanation: Bucket machines drag a bucket through large sewers and physically haul out heavy material such as sand, gravel, and compacted debris that water jets cannot suspend and move.
options: In a small diameter house lateral
When the blockage is only light grease film
In a large sewer with heavy deposits of sand, gravel, and debris that jetting cannot move effectively
When no downstream access exists at all
optionA: In a small diameter house lateral
optionB: When the blockage is only light grease film
optionC: In a large sewer with heavy deposits of sand, gravel, and debris that jetting cannot move effectively
optionD: When no downstream access exists at all
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: During jetting, why should loosened debris be captured and removed at the downstream manhole instead of being flushed further down the system?
correctAnswer: Material left in the flow can resettle and cause a blockage in a downstream reach
explanation: Debris flushed downstream is not removed from the system. When velocity drops it resettles, often at the next flat reach or obstruction, and creates a new blockage.
options: Material left in the flow can resettle and cause a blockage in a downstream reach
Debris damages the water in the sewer
The jetting hose cannot push debris at all
Downstream pipes are always smaller
optionA: Material left in the flow can resettle and cause a blockage in a downstream reach
optionB: Debris damages the water in the sewer
optionC: The jetting hose cannot push debris at all
optionD: Downstream pipes are always smaller

question: A crew jets a reach and flow improves, but the same reach blocks again within weeks, twice in a row. What is the best next step?
correctAnswer: Inspect the reach with CCTV to find the underlying cause, such as roots or a structural defect
explanation: Rapid repeat blockages after proper cleaning point to a cause that cleaning cannot fix, such as root intrusion at a joint or a cracked, offset, or sagging pipe. CCTV inspection identifies the defect so a repair can be planned.
options: Jet the reach on the same schedule forever without investigating
Reduce the pipe size so velocity rises
Stop cleaning and wait for a complaint
Inspect the reach with CCTV to find the underlying cause, such as roots or a structural defect
optionA: Jet the reach on the same schedule forever without investigating
optionB: Reduce the pipe size so velocity rises
optionC: Stop cleaning and wait for a complaint
optionD: Inspect the reach with CCTV to find the underlying cause, such as roots or a structural defect
sourceTitle: US EPA - CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Why is rodding sometimes chosen for a blockage caused by a dense root mass in a small sewer?
correctAnswer: The rotating rods and cutting head can cut through and retrieve material that water jets may not clear
explanation: A rodding machine drives rotating rods with a cutting head that can cut and pull out dense obstructions such as root masses, which a water jet may only punch a small hole through.
options: Rodding disinfects the pipe as it works
The rotating rods and cutting head can cut through and retrieve material that water jets may not clear
Rodding works without any access point
Rodding increases the diameter of the pipe permanently
optionA: Rodding disinfects the pipe as it works
optionB: The rotating rods and cutting head can cut through and retrieve material that water jets may not clear
optionC: Rodding works without any access point
optionD: Rodding increases the diameter of the pipe permanently

question: Before a worker enters a manhole, which atmospheric testing is required as part of entry preparation?
correctAnswer: Test for oxygen, flammable gases, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon monoxide, before entry and during the entry
explanation: Manholes and other collection system spaces can contain oxygen deficient air, flammable gas, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon monoxide. Testing before entry and monitoring during entry are core preparation steps under confined space practice.
options: Test only for oxygen, since other gases are rare
Test only after the worker reports a smell
Test for oxygen, flammable gases, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon monoxide, before entry and during the entry
No testing is needed if the manhole was open all day
optionA: Test only for oxygen, since other gases are rare
optionB: Test only after the worker reports a smell
optionC: Test for oxygen, flammable gases, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon monoxide, before entry and during the entry
optionD: No testing is needed if the manhole was open all day
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Confined Spaces

question: What is the attendant's role during a confined space entry into a wet well?
correctAnswer: Stay outside the space, keep contact with the entrant, and start rescue procedures without entering the space
explanation: The attendant remains outside, maintains communication, monitors conditions, and initiates the rescue plan. The attendant must never enter the space, because would be rescuers entering without protection are a common cause of multiple fatalities.
options: Stay outside the space, keep contact with the entrant, and start rescue procedures without entering the space
Enter the space with the worker to hold the light
Leave to fetch tools once entry begins
Enter the space first if the entrant calls for help
optionA: Stay outside the space, keep contact with the entrant, and start rescue procedures without entering the space
optionB: Enter the space with the worker to hold the light
optionC: Leave to fetch tools once entry begins
optionD: Enter the space first if the entrant calls for help

question: Why is forced air ventilation run before and during entry into a manhole?
correctAnswer: To supply clean air and keep the atmosphere within safe limits for the whole entry
explanation: Forced air ventilation with clean air dilutes and removes hazardous gases and maintains oxygen, and it must continue during the entry because conditions in a sewer can change while work is underway.
options: To dry the walls before inspection
To cool the pump motors below
To push wastewater through the sewer faster
To supply clean air and keep the atmosphere within safe limits for the whole entry
optionA: To dry the walls before inspection
optionB: To cool the pump motors below
optionC: To push wastewater through the sewer faster
optionD: To supply clean air and keep the atmosphere within safe limits for the whole entry
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Confined Spaces

question: Which setup provides non entry rescue for a worker in a vertical manhole entry?
correctAnswer: A tripod over the opening with a winch and a full body harness on the entrant
explanation: A tripod, winch, and harness let the attendant or rescue team lift an incapacitated entrant straight out of a vertical space without anyone entering, which is the preferred rescue method.
options: A ladder and a rope tied to a truck bumper
A tripod over the opening with a winch and a full body harness on the entrant
A second worker waiting inside the space
A ventilation blower used as a lifting device
optionA: A ladder and a rope tied to a truck bumper
optionB: A tripod over the opening with a winch and a full body harness on the entrant
optionC: A second worker waiting inside the space
optionD: A ventilation blower used as a lifting device

question: Why is hydrogen sulfide especially dangerous in a sewer manhole?
correctAnswer: It can collect in low areas and, at higher concentrations, quickly dull the sense of smell so workers stop detecting it
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide is produced by decomposing sewage and tends to collect in low, still areas of a space. At higher concentrations it paralyzes the sense of smell, removing the warning odour and exposing workers to a toxic atmosphere.
options: It is lighter than air and escapes before entry
It has a strong warning smell at all concentrations
It can collect in low areas and, at higher concentrations, quickly dull the sense of smell so workers stop detecting it
It is only a hazard in drinking water systems
optionA: It is lighter than air and escapes before entry
optionB: It has a strong warning smell at all concentrations
optionC: It can collect in low areas and, at higher concentrations, quickly dull the sense of smell so workers stop detecting it
optionD: It is only a hazard in drinking water systems
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide
